articles.headline: Indian hockey teams begin Asian Games with crushing wins
articles.summary: The Indian men's hockey team opened their Asian Games campaign with a dominant 13-1 victory over Uzbekistan. Simultaneously, the women's team also launched their campaign in a ruthless fashion, hammering Uzbekistan 19-0. These massive wins establish India as a primary gold medal contender in both categories.

articles.headline: 48-year-old man beaten to death by neighbours over construction dispute
articles.summary: A 48-year-old property dealer was allegedly beaten to death in South Delhi's Kalkaji following a dispute over an extended residential area. The clash broke out between residents of a building on Saturday night. Police have arrested three suspects, while three others remain on the run. The incident highlights rising urban local violence in the capital.

articles.headline: Delhi proposes extension for fire service rules until February 2025
articles.summary: The Delhi government has proposed a three-month extension for implementing the Delhi Fire Service (Amendment) Rules, 2025. The delay follows concerns over the eligibility of third-party fire safety auditors. The proposal will be sent to Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena for final approval to ensure compliance in high-risk residential and commercial buildings.

articles.headline: Naga film 'Angh' bags Oscars berth with global festival prize
articles.summary: The Naga film 'Angh,' directed by Theja Rio, won the prestigious Platform Prize at the Toronto International Film Festival, making it eligible for the Oscars. Set in the 1960s, the film explores Naga culture and resistance against missionary influence. It is the first time an Indian film has secured this specific global recognition at TIFF.

articles.headline: Top Maoist commander gunned down in Uttar Pradesh police encounter
articles.summary: Brijesh Ganjhu, a top Maoist commander carrying a ₹30 lakh bounty, was killed in an encounter with the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) near Varanasi. Ganjhu was wanted in at least 44 cases of murder and extortion across UP and Jharkhand. Police recovered automatic weapons and ammunition from the site following the early morning gunfight.

articles.headline: DigiYatra for international air travel to launch in Delhi, Mumbai
articles.summary: The Indian government is planning to extend the DigiYatra facial-recognition system to international departures by December. Delhi and Mumbai airports will be the first to roll out the service. The system will use e-passports for seamless entry, security, and boarding, though emigration checks will remain manual in the initial phase to ensure security compliance.

articles.headline: Akal Takht excommunicates SAD leader following rape allegations
articles.summary: The Akal Takht has excommunicated SAD leader and SGPC member Amarjit Singh Chawla following allegations of rape. The decision was taken by five high priests after a Bahrain-based woman accused Chawla of raping her at a gurdwara in Sangrur. Chawla has been divested of all religious and political positions within the Sikh community until cleared of the charges.

articles.headline: Global military spending rises to record $2.77 trillion in 2025
articles.summary: A report on the economics of munitions reveals that global military expenditure reached $2.77 trillion in 2025, a 41% increase since 2015. The surge is driven by conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia, leading to a shift toward low-cost drones and mass-produced munitions. India has emerged as a significant producer, with domestic production reaching ₹1.78 lakh crore.

articles.headline: Floods in Kerala's Malappuram leave two dead, others missing
articles.summary: Two people were killed and two others remain missing after heavy rains triggered flash floods in Kerala's Malappuram district. The victims were swept away while crossing a bridge at Nilambur. Search and rescue operations are ongoing by Fire and Rescue Services. The state has been put on alert as the weather department predicts more heavy rainfall in the region.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping and Donald Trump to hold talks on trade
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to arrive in Washington for high-stakes talks with Donald Trump. Key issues on the table include a trade truce extension, tariff reliefs, and AI safety regulations. The meeting comes as both economies face pressure from cooling growth and rising inflation, with the US seeking further concessions on agricultural and energy exports.

articles.headline: Election Commission issues notices to 3.3 million Delhi voters
articles.summary: The Election Commission has sent notices to 3.3 million voters in Delhi after identifying discrepancies in the draft electoral roll. The issues include 'no mapping' to previous records, multiple listings, and mismatched details. Officials clarified that receiving a notice does not mean immediate deletion but is part of a verification process to ensure roll accuracy.

articles.headline: Bengaluru liveability index shows rise in jobs and food prices
articles.summary: A monthly liveability index for Bengaluru shows that formal sector jobs grew by 8% in July 2026, reaching 5.8 million employees. However, the city faced a rise in food prices, particularly rice and onions. While air quality remained 'satisfactory,' domestic air traffic saw an 11% dip, reflecting shifting urban economic patterns in India's IT hub.

articles.headline: No immediate ban on student politics at Kerala University
articles.summary: Kerala's Higher Education Minister R Bindu clarified that the state has not taken a decision to ban student politics at Kerala University. The statement follows a draft code of conduct that proposed restrictions on political activities to maintain campus discipline. The minister emphasized that student unions should be allowed to function as part of the democratic process.

articles.headline: FDA cancels 16 drug licenses in Karnataka over counterfeit concerns
articles.summary: Karnataka's Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cancelled 16 and suspended 8 drug licenses following a probe into counterfeit medicines. The action targeted pharmacies and wholesalers found selling misbranded medications. This follows an August raid on an unlicensed facility where fake labels and packaging for major pharmaceutical brands were discovered.

articles.headline: India and Japan bolster defense ties through joint fighter training
articles.summary: The Air Chiefs of India and Japan met in Jodhpur to review joint training and operational exercises. The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral defense cooperation and enhancing interoperability between the two air forces. Both nations committed to expanding the scope of their defense partnership to address shared security challenges in the Indo-Pacific region.

articles.headline: IIT Bombay students demand resignation of director after campus protests
articles.summary: Students at IIT Bombay have demanded the resignation of the institute’s director following a series of protests. The unrest began after the death of a student and subsequent allegations of inadequate counseling and health services. Students are calling for better mental health support, 24/7 psychiatric services, and student representation in campus decision-making bodies.

articles.headline: India-Bangladesh trade task force to promote bilateral economic ties
articles.summary: India and Bangladesh have agreed to set up a joint task force to promote bilateral trade and investment. The initiative aims to reduce trade barriers, improve logistical connectivity, and encourage cross-border entrepreneurship. The task force will focus on sectors like textiles, energy, and digital services to enhance economic cooperation between the two neighbors.

articles.headline: Petrol benchmark hits 50-month high as global oil prices surge
articles.summary: India's petrol pricing benchmark has risen to a 50-month high of $133.05 per barrel, driven by supply disruptions in West Asia and a global energy crunch. The surge has led to a hike in domestic petrol and diesel prices by approximately ₹5 per litre. Oil marketing companies warn of further volatility if regional tensions in the Middle East continue to escalate.

articles.headline: RBI approves record ₹2.11 lakh crore dividend for the central government
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India’s board has approved a record surplus transfer of ₹2,10,874 crore to the central government for fiscal year 2023-24. This payout is more than double the government's budget estimate of ₹1.02 lakh crore, providing a massive fiscal boost that could help narrow the fiscal deficit or increase capital expenditure.

articles.headline: India flash PMI data signals strong expansion in manufacturing and services
articles.summary: The HSBC Flash India Composite PMI rose to a near 14-year high of 61.7 in May, up from 61.5 in April. The data indicates a significant acceleration in the private sector, driven by robust new orders and strong international demand, reinforcing India's position as one of the fastest-growing major economies.

articles.headline: Sensex and Nifty hit record highs following RBI dividend boost
articles.summary: Indian equity benchmarks Sensex and Nifty 50 surged to fresh all-time highs on Wednesday. Investor sentiment was bolstered by the RBI’s announcement of a massive dividend payout, which exceeded market expectations and is expected to improve the government's fiscal health and reduce sovereign borrowing needs.

articles.headline: Election Commission warns parties against using children in political campaigns
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India has issued a directive to political parties to refrain from involving children in election-related activities. The poll body cited the Model Code of Conduct and the Child Labour Act, warning that strict action would be taken against any party using minors for leafleting or campaign rallies.

articles.headline: Severe heatwave across North India pushes power demand to seasonal record
articles.summary: A persistent heatwave has gripped several states in Northern and Central India, with temperatures crossing 47 degrees Celsius in various districts. The weather department has issued a red alert for the region, warning of severe health risks and the impact of the prolonged extreme heat on labor productivity and water supply.

articles.headline: India peak power demand hits record high amid searing summer heatwave
articles.summary: The national peak power demand reached a seasonal record of 237 GW on Wednesday as intense heat drove up the use of cooling appliances. The Power Ministry stated that it is coordinating with state utilities and coal suppliers to ensure uninterrupted supply, although the surge is testing the capacity of the national grid.

articles.headline: Supreme Court clarifies arrest procedures under the PMLA for trial courts
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that the Enforcement Directorate cannot arrest an accused once a trial court has taken cognizance of the complaint, provided the individual was not arrested during the investigation. The court emphasized that the agency must apply for custody through the court rather than exercising summary arrest powers.

articles.headline: Global investors await Nvidia Q1 results as AI demand fuels tech
articles.summary: Technology markets are focused on Nvidia’s upcoming quarterly earnings report, which serves as a major indicator for the global AI boom. Analysts expect substantial revenue growth driven by data center chip demand, with the results likely to influence broad market sentiment across the global technology sector.

articles.headline: US Fed minutes show cautious approach to future interest rate cuts
articles.summary: Minutes from the latest Federal Reserve meeting indicate that officials remain concerned about persistent inflation and believe it will take longer than previously thought to gain the confidence needed to cut interest rates. The stance suggests that the U.S. central bank will maintain higher rates for an extended period.

articles.headline: Kolkata Knight Riders beat Sunrisers Hyderabad to reach IPL 2024 final
articles.summary: Kolkata Knight Riders secured their spot in the IPL 2024 final with a dominant eight-wicket win over Sunrisers Hyderabad in Qualifier 1. A stellar bowling performance led by Mitchell Starc followed by half-centuries from Venkatesh Iyer and Shreyas Iyer ensured KKR's comfortable victory at the Narendra Modi Stadium.

articles.headline: Higher Education Institutions Must Prioritize Research and Innovation Over Admissions
articles.summary: This article argues that Indian higher education institutions should shift focus from admissions and placements to knowledge creation, research, and innovation. It emphasizes four pillars: research publications, scholarly books, patents, and funded projects, to strengthen institutional profiles, foster collaboration, and address real-world challenges, contributing to societal progress and a global knowledge hub.

articles.headline: Career Guidance for Graduates in Tech, Law, and Language Translation
articles.summary: This column offers career advice to graduates. Sanskar, with degrees in Anthropology and English Literature, is advised on tech niches like Data Analytics and AI. Anshula, with BBA and LL.B, gets guidance on international law/policy careers. Sahil, studying Urdu, receives tips for language translation jobs in media, tech, and government, including CAT tools and international opportunities. Devika, interested in defence, is told sports certificates aid SSB but exams are mandatory.

articles.headline: Indian Universities Face Challenge in Integrating AI Ethics into Curriculum
articles.summary: As AI reshapes industries, Indian universities, while building technical AI capacity, are failing to adequately embed ethical training. Current AI education often treats ethics as a compliance checkbox, leading to dangerous gaps in high-stakes decisions. The article suggests integrating ethics into technical courses, fostering judgment through case studies and public-interest projects, and aligning employer expectations and accreditation standards to produce ethical AI leaders.

articles.headline: UNICEF and Bitget Launch Online Financial Literacy Module for Youth
articles.summary: Bitget and UNICEF partnered to create an online financial literacy module for the Game Changers Coalition curriculum. The free, self-paced course, available via Agora, covers budgeting, credit, loans, interest, and blockchain using videos and quizzes. Participants receive a certificate upon completion, aiming to educate young learners on essential money matters.

articles.headline: Strategic Skipping Crucial for Success in CAT Examination
articles.summary: This article advises CAT aspirants to master strategic skipping, emphasizing that a 99 percentile often requires attempting only 50-55% of the paper. By intentionally relinquishing difficult questions, candidates can double time for solvable ones, increasing accuracy. The strategy differs by section: immediate decision for VARC, block evaluation for DILR, and timed chunks for QA, focusing on strengths and avoiding new complex topics.

articles.headline: U.S. Visa Rules for International Students Undergo Significant Changes
articles.summary: Recent U.S. visa changes will impact international students. The Duration of Status (D/S) for F-1 visas will be replaced by a fixed four-year admission period from September 15, 2026, requiring formal extension applications. The grace period for Optional Practical Training (OPT) applications is reduced from 60 to 30 days. Stricter CPT interpretation aims to prevent misuse. A proposed $100,000 OPT fee is under consideration but faces significant opposition, raising concerns about its economic impact.

articles.headline: India's Real Estate Boom Creates Diverse Career Opportunities for Students
articles.summary: India's commercial real estate industry, driven by Global Capability Centres and demand for quality office spaces, is evolving, creating new career paths. Educational institutions are designing courses covering real estate, hospitality operations, and technology, integrating experiential learning and professional certifications. New roles include Workplace Experience Manager and Sustainability Coordinator. Graduates from various backgrounds like Business, Hospitality, and Engineering can pursue these careers by developing technical, interpersonal, and digital literacy skills.

articles.headline: Young Equestrian Develops AI System for Early Horse Pain Detection
articles.summary: Sanya Sharma, a young equestrian, developed "EquiSense AI," a CREST Gold Award-winning project, to detect early signs of pain or stress in horses. Her system combines heart rate, inertial motion, temperature, and skin response sensors with a machine learning model. It classifies a horse's state (calm, stressed, in pain, at risk of colic/lameness/heat stress) and explains its findings for vet verification. The prototype is being piloted at Sterling Stables, which has placed an order.

articles.headline: Indian Women's Table Tennis Team Scripts Comeback Win
articles.summary: India's women's table tennis team achieved a 3-2 comeback victory over Singapore in Group F, but the men's team suffered a 0-3 loss to Iran. Both teams began their campaigns with identical 3-0 wins against Indonesia.

articles.headline: Atletico Madrid Beats 10-Man Real, Man City Wins 8-Goal Thriller
articles.summary: Atletico Madrid won 2-1 against 10-man Real Madrid in a Spanish league derby. Manchester City prevailed 5-3 against Sunderland in an eight-goal thriller to move clear at the top of the Premier League.

articles.headline: Indian Men Win Chess Olympiad; Women Shocked by Poland
articles.summary: The Indian men's chess team, led by R Praggnanandhaa and D Gukesh, achieved an emphatic 3-1 victory over Holland in the 46th Chess Olympiad. However, the Indian women's team was shocked by Poland, losing 1.5-2.5.

articles.headline: Alexander Zverev Leads Germany into Davis Cup Final 8
articles.summary: Newly crowned US Open champion Alexander Zverev sent Germany into the Davis Cup Final 8 by easing past Croatia's Dino Prizmic 6-2, 6-4. Britain, Austria, Canada, South Korea, and the Czech Republic also progressed.

articles.headline: Indian Economy Shows Strong 7.8% Q1 Growth Amid Debate
articles.summary: India's GDP grew 7.8% in Q1 FY27, sparking debate on whether gains are felt on the ground. Analysis shows strong investments, robust factory and services activity despite West Asia-related headwinds and rising input costs.

articles.headline: Indian HNIs Face Forex, Tax Issues with SpaceX Share Transfers
articles.summary: Many rich Indians holding unlisted SpaceX shares, acquired through offshore funds and vehicles, are grappling with questions about preserving their fortune. They seek legal advice on whether their investments comply with complex forex and tax regulations after in-specie transfers.

articles.headline: Chip Companies to Invest in India Within Six Months, Says Vaishnaw
articles.summary: Union Minister for Electronics and IT Ashwini Vaishnaw announced that several chip companies are expected to start investments in India within six months, leveraging the $23.5 billion committed under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM 2.0).

articles.headline: AI Companies Bear Bigger Responsibility for Safety, Says Vaishnaw
articles.summary: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw states AI companies have a "much bigger responsibility" to build safeguards within their models due to the rapid development pace and potential risks. He advocates for a techno-legal framework.

articles.headline: Trump Sons-Linked Powerus Signs Anti-Drone Deals in India, Pakistan
articles.summary: US drone company Powerus, linked to Donald Trump's sons, signed a licensing pact to make anti-drone systems with an Indian firm, Paras Defence. Months later, it inked a deal to sell armed drones to Pakistan's military.

articles.headline: Congress Urges India to Reject US Tariffs on Russian Oil
articles.summary: Congress slams US President Trump's bill enabling 100% tariffs on Russian oil buyers, including India. It urges the Centre to reject the move and halt trade deal talks until tariff issues are resolved, citing US hypocrisy.

articles.headline: J&K Opposition Gears Up to Challenge Omar Government
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir opposition parties, including BJP and PDP, are set to corner the ruling National Conference government over governance failures, reservation policy, and statehood during the assembly session starting today.

articles.headline: Crime Branch Probes IIT-B Student Suicide, Father Alleges Caste Harassment
articles.summary: Mumbai Crime Branch has taken over the probe into an IIT Bombay student's suicide. His father alleges caste-based harassment and mental torture by a faculty member, a claim denied by the institute's dean.

articles.headline: Japanese Fighters Operate from Indian Soil in Joint Exercise
articles.summary: Japanese fighter aircraft are operating from Indian soil for the first time in a bilateral air exercise, Veer Guardian 2026, marking a major milestone in defence cooperation between India and Japan.

articles.headline: Herd of 40 Elephants Causes Panic Near Jharkhand Coal Mines
articles.summary: A herd of around 40 elephants roaming near Central Coalfields Limited mines in Ramgarh, Jharkhand, has triggered panic among miners and villagers, prompting increased vigilance to prevent human-animal conflict.

articles.headline: Manipur Woman Succumbs to Gun Injuries After Attack
articles.summary: A 21-year-old woman, Nei Esther Gangte, died at Churachandpur District Hospital in Manipur after battling critical injuries for seven days, following a gun attack by armed miscreants.

articles.headline: Pitbull Attacks Class 7 Student, Causes 16 Bites
articles.summary: A pitbull dog attacked a Class 7 student in Faridabad, biting him 16 times and leaving him seriously wounded. The dog's owner allegedly made no attempt to intervene, according to a police complaint.

articles.headline: ED Probes TMC's `5.22 Crore Advance for Unused Aviation Services
articles.summary: The ED is examining `5.22 crore in advance payments by Trinamool Congress for aviation services for July-September 2026. The services covered by payments had not been availed, as part of a wider probe into the party's finances.

articles.headline: Karnataka to Send All-Party Delegation to PM on Western Ghats ESA
articles.summary: Karnataka plans to send an all-party delegation to PM Modi to convey its strong reservations against declaring parts of the Western Ghats as an Eco-Sensitive Area (ESA). The state fears adverse impacts on livelihoods and will formulate its response in a special assembly session.

articles.headline: TMC Office, Leaders' Homes Vandalised in Kolkata's Jadavpur
articles.summary: A TMC office, the residences of a former MLA and councillor, and a CPI(M) memorial were allegedly vandalised in Jadavpur, south Kolkata. TMC and Left parties accuse BJP workers; BJP denies involvement, citing internal TMC dispute.

articles.headline: Prominent Figures Get Notices for Voter Detail Discrepancies
articles.summary: LK Advani, S Jaishankar, SS Sandhu, and Arvind Kejriwal are among the many prominent figures issued notices for "discrepancies" in voter details under the Delhi Special Integrated Revision (SIR) exercise, including late economist Bibek Debroy.

articles.headline: Bengal CM Says Kurmi Tribal Community Excluded from UCC Bill
articles.summary: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari stated that the Kurmi tribal community in Purulia will be excluded from the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) bill. This decision was made following requests from tribal leaders concerned about their customary laws.

articles.headline: 1.59 Lakh Voters Excluded from Nagaland Electoral Draft Roll
articles.summary: Nagaland's draft electoral roll excludes nearly 1.59 lakh voters from the pre-SIR list of 13.57 lakh. Reasons include deceased, absent, shifted, or multiple enrollments, according to the Chief Electoral Officer's office.

articles.headline: BJP Attacks Rahul Gandhi Over Stand-up Act Insulting PM's Mother
articles.summary: BJP demanded an apology from Rahul Gandhi after a comedian mimicked PM Modi's style and insulted his mother at a Congress event. Congress leader Raashid Alvi defended it as mimicry, citing PM Modi's past remarks about Sonia Gandhi.

articles.headline: Regional Parties Explore Forming Non-BJP, Non-Congress Political Front
articles.summary: Regional parties like DMK, TMC, Shiv Sena (UBT), and NCP(SP) are discussing forming a non-BJP, non-Congress front nationally. A parallel initiative is gathering pace in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the assembly elections, involving AIMIM, Azad Samaj Party, and others.

articles.headline: Inox Clean Energy Nears `2,500 Crore Acquisition of Athena Renewables
articles.summary: Inox Clean Energy is close to acquiring Actis-backed Athena Renewables for an enterprise value of `2,500 crore. This acquisition, nearing conclusion, would expand Inox's total operational renewable energy capacity to nearly 5 GW.

articles.headline: Banks to Standardize Project Finance Lending Norms After RBI Guidelines
articles.summary: Indian banks are developing a common framework for project finance lending to align norms on capital outlay, funding amount, and gestation period. This initiative aims to curb regulatory arbitrage and operational misalignment among consortium lenders following RBI guidelines.

articles.headline: ICAI Proposes CA Act Changes to Create Larger Accounting Firms
articles.summary: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) is preparing proposals to amend the CA Act, aiming for measured deregulation of non-assurance services. This seeks to foster larger Indian accounting and consulting firms capable of competing with global 'Big-4' firms.

articles.headline: JLR Seeks £1 Billion Loan Amid Tata Group Leadership Uncertainty
articles.summary: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) is in talks with global banks for a £1 billion five-year term loan. Lenders are discussing leadership uncertainty at Tata Group due to Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata's opposition to N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons chairman.

articles.headline: Protein Demand Fuels Collaborations and M&A in Food Sector
articles.summary: A surge in consumer demand for protein in India is driving collaborations among food and beverage makers and cafe chains, alongside M&A activity. This occurs despite global shortages and a four-fold increase in whey protein prices.

articles.headline: SP Group Backs Tata Sons Listing Plan After Stake Sale Delay
articles.summary: The Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group is backing a Tata Sons listing after its proposed 2.5% stake sale, intended to monetize part of its holding, was delayed. This comes post an RBI directive on listing for upper-layer NBFCs.

articles.headline: Magnum to Reformulate Products Amid GLP-1 Drugs and AI Impact
articles.summary: Magnum Ice Cream Co. plans to reformulate products for protein, hydration, and sugar reduction, driven by GLP-1 drugs and AI-powered shopping influencing food consumption, especially in India, China, and the US, says CEO Peter ter Kulve.

articles.headline: Oil Prices Key External Risk, But India's Growth Outlook Resilient
articles.summary: Rising oil prices and energy transit disruptions pose key external risks, but India's growth remains resilient. This is attributed to diversified crude sourcing and RBI's foreign reserves buffer, according to DBS Bank.

articles.headline: India Needs Structural Growth Beyond Policy Support, Says HSBC Economist
articles.summary: Pranjul Bhandari of HSBC states India's current strong growth is cyclical and needs to become more structural. She highlights the need for ease of doing business, policy certainty, regulatory improvements, and better infrastructure, especially for mid-tech exports.

articles.headline: Bengal Needs Unambiguous Intent to Build Industry, Not Shallow Politics
articles.summary: West Bengal is debating land assembly for industry. The article argues that attracting capital requires confidence in institutional credibility, consistent policy, and genuine intent for industrialization, moving beyond political rhetoric, not just agitation.

articles.headline: Jürgen Klopp Urges Germans to Reclaim Positive National Pride
articles.summary: Germany's football coach Jürgen Klopp advocates for reclaiming national pride from extremists, distinguishing healthy patriotism ("I love my country") from unhealthy nationalism, a lesson applicable beyond Germany, as he wants to "reclaim the flag."

articles.headline: Women Investors Slowly Rising in India's Stock Market
articles.summary: The share of women among individual investors registered with the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in India is slowly rising, reaching 25.1% from 22.6% at the end of FY22. Goa, Mizoram, Sikkim, Delhi, and Nagaland show the highest shares.

articles.headline: Sebi May Allow Settlement in Fund Diversion Cases with Restitution
articles.summary: India's capital market regulator, Sebi, plans to allow companies and individuals accused of siphoning funds to settle cases if they return diverted money with interest and make appropriate disclosures. This marks a shift to a more pragmatic enforcement framework.

articles.headline: Sun Life CEO Kevin Strain Discusses FDI, Bancassurance, and AI
articles.summary: Sun Life's CEO Kevin Strain speaks on foreign direct investment opportunities, challenges in bancassurance, trends in asset management companies, and the impact of artificial intelligence in an exclusive interview.

articles.headline: Sensex Records Longest Stretch Without New High Since 2012
articles.summary: The BSE Sensex has endured 725 days without a new record high since September 26, 2024, marking its longest stretch since 2012. This two-year period of flattish returns is testing investors' patience, despite only a 13.4% fall from its peak.

articles.headline: IPO Market Heats Up with 20 Companies Launching Issues
articles.summary: The primary market is buzzing with activity as seven mainboard and 13 SME initial public offerings (IPOs) are scheduled for subscription this week, with a combined issue size of `4,152 crore, extending the fundraising momentum.

articles.headline: India Must Focus on Semiconductor Design Ecosystem, Says Vaishnaw
articles.summary: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw emphasizes building India's semiconductor design ecosystem, providing latest design tools to institutions, and attracting precision manufacturing to serve multiple industries like aeronautical, space, and defense.

articles.headline: Emergent Expands AI Automation to Small Businesses with AI Agents
articles.summary: AI startup Emergent is expanding from app building to automating day-to-day functions for small businesses using AI agents for tasks like cash-flow analysis and social media management. The goal is autonomous operations for businesses.

articles.headline: CityMall Seeks `400-500 Crore Funding Round at `4,000 Crore Valuation
articles.summary: Value e-commerce startup CityMall, focusing on non-metro customers, is in talks to raise `400-500 crore in fresh funding, led by existing investor Jungle Ventures, at an expected valuation of `4,000 crore. The company eyes an IPO in 6-8 quarters.

articles.headline: Chinese Chipmaker CXMT Begins Mass Production of 5th-Gen DRAM
articles.summary: Chinese DRAM chipmaker CXMT announced mass production of its fifth-generation technology platform, a claimed breakthrough poised to boost China's competition with global memory chip giants like Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.

articles.headline: Oracle's $18 Billion Data Centre Debt Faces Pressure
articles.summary: About $18 billion in loans tied to an Oracle-leased data centre in New Mexico are under pressure. Growing local opposition over water supply and air quality concerns could derail Oracle's massive AI infrastructure build-out.

articles.headline: Chipmakers Adopt 'Security by Design' for AI in Cloud Transition
articles.summary: Chipmakers are integrating "security by design" deeper into chip design to guard against growing cyberattack risks. This is driven by the increasing volume of data moving between AI-connected devices and cloud systems, with tighter norms being imposed.

articles.headline: Silicon Valley Fears AI's Existential Threat, India Fears Job Loss
articles.summary: While Silicon Valley engineers worry about AI's potential to threaten humanity, Indian AI startup founders report that their engineers are more concerned about AI taking away jobs and making their skills less valuable.

articles.headline: Open PLI Scheme to Smaller Firms Can Drive Green Transition
articles.summary: IIT-Madras professor Ashok Jhunjhunwala advocates for reviewing India's Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. He suggests including smaller companies and incentivizing meaningful domestic value addition, not just assembly, to drive green transition.

articles.headline: Major AI Companies Sued Over Alleged 'AI Slowdown' Agreement
articles.summary: Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google face a lawsuit alleging they made an illegal agreement to slow AI development. The suit claims this reduces consumer value for paid subscriptions and violates trust laws.

articles.headline: Indian Corporates Actively Tap Bond Market Amid Rate Hike Buzz
articles.summary: Indian companies are actively tapping the bond market, taking advantage of surplus liquidity to lock in funding before potential interest rate hikes and tighter liquidity conditions. Several large issues, exceeding `1,000 crore, are planned for this week.

articles.headline: Tata Trusts Prepared to Fund Legal Challenge Against Tata Sons Board Decisions
articles.summary: Tata Trusts is prepared to fund legal costs for challenging the Tata Sons board's decisions on N Chandrasekaran's reappointment. The Trusts assert majority shareholder rights, amid differing views among some trustees regarding the legal approach.

articles.headline: SIP Additions Hit Six-Month High, But Discontinuations Also Rise
articles.summary: Net additions to Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) accounts reached a six-month high in August. However, the year-on-year rate of increase remained volatile due to a faster pace of SIP discontinuations, reflecting market volatility and investor behavior.

articles.headline: Iran Warns of Wider Retaliation Against US, Allies
articles.summary: Iran's military warned of sustained retaliation against US bases and regional allies if the US and its allies launch a new attack. Iran cites intelligence that such a move is being prepared, escalating Middle East tensions.

articles.headline: US, China Hold Trade Talks Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit
articles.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng will lead trade talks in New York, laying groundwork for a Trump-Xi summit. Discussions will cover trade, energy, and AI, aiming to maintain stability in their tariff truce.

articles.headline: Turkey Signals Military Support for Saudi Arabia Against Houthis
articles.summary: Turkey’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan signalled technical military support for Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks in Yemen, in line with the Mecca Defence Alliance. Saudi Arabia is facing intensifying attacks, drawing it deeper into regional conflict.

articles.headline: Denmark Affirms Greenland Sovereignty Intact Under US Military Deal
articles.summary: Denmark stated its sovereignty over Greenland would not be compromised by a deal with the Trump administration to expand the US military presence there. The agreement aims to prevent adversaries from establishing bases on the Arctic island.

articles.headline: India and Vietnam Boost Flight Capacity with New Aviation Deal
articles.summary: India and Vietnam have agreed to more than double bilateral air capacity to over 16,000 seats per week, from the current 8,000. This follows strong demand and will allow airlines like Vietnam Airlines and IndiGo to add more flights to Indian metros.

articles.headline: Aragen Life Sciences Boosts Investment in Complex Drug Modalities
articles.summary: Hyderabad-based CRDMO Aragen Life Sciences is investing in complex drug modalities like Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs), peptides, and high-potent APIs. This aims to move up the drug development and manufacturing value chain, expanding capacity.

articles.headline: Why Apple faces CCPA probe over user-rights issue
articles.summary: India's Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) is probing Apple's software warranty terms after iOS 18 updates allegedly caused hardware failures, leaving users with repair bills. The CCPA is examining if this constitutes unfair trade practice, potentially impacting other phone makers' warranty policies.

articles.headline: Open split in Tata Group casts light on Venu Srinivasan's role
articles.summary: An open split within the Tata Group highlights Tata Sons director Venu Srinivasan's controversial role. His backing of N. Chandrasekaran's third term and changed stance on Tata Sons' listing, alongside allegations of trust rule breaches and conflict of interest, have created a crisis within the conglomerate.

articles.headline: Key economic data releases and policy cues to watch this week
articles.summary: This week's economic watch includes RBI's credit/deposit data, September flash PMI, August core industries output for India. From the US, Fed officials' comments on rate paths will be tracked amid rising oil prices. Foreign tourist arrival data will also reveal India's tourism standing.

articles.headline: Coforge, Hexaware help clients manage AI token budgets
articles.summary: IT firms Coforge and Hexaware are helping clients navigate massive AI token bills by managing usage and rethinking pricing. Coforge focuses on model choice and open-weight AI, while Hexaware offers token-based pricing, addressing a common issue where clients burn through annual token budgets in months.

articles.headline: Samara Capital creates integrated logistics platform with new acquisitions
articles.summary: Samara Capital invested ₹1,200 crore to create an integrated logistics platform by acquiring stakes in Associated Road Carriers (ARC) and Calyx Container Terminals. The combined entity, with ₹2,140 crore revenue, will expand network, strengthen first- and last-mile capabilities, modernize tech, and pursue acquisitions in India's growing logistics sector.

articles.headline: Serum Institute invests ₹250 crore in Yotta Data Services
articles.summary: Vaccine maker Serum Institute of India (SII) invested ₹250 crore in Yotta Data Services' ₹1,396 crore July fundraise, valuing the company at ₹37,000 crore. Dovetail Financial Services and Asio Fund VCC were also significant investors, fueling Yotta's expansion as Indian conglomerates ramp up data-centre investments.

articles.headline: FSSAI chief warns food industry to prioritize consumer safety
articles.summary: FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani announced tighter scrutiny for online food businesses, emphasizing clear information for consumers, warning symbols on packaged foods for sugar, salt, and fat levels, and stronger enforcement. He stated the industry 'has no choice' but to comply, extending regulation to schools and online platforms amidst rising complaints.

articles.headline: Nilon’s explores majority stake sale valuing firm at ₹800-1,200 crore
articles.summary: Pune-based Nilon’s, a packaged foods company, is exploring a majority stake sale, potentially valuing it at ₹800-1,200 crore. Several strategic and private equity firms have been approached. The founding family may continue overseeing operations, while existing investors consider a partial or full exit.

articles.headline: Centre plans central calendar to streamline job exams
articles.summary: The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) is spearheading a new plan to streamline annual competitive examinations across central government departments. The initiative aims to avoid scheduling conflicts, reduce delays, and bring predictability to public sector recruitment, which impacts millions of job aspirants.

articles.headline: PwC India's consulting unit merges with PwC US Advisory
articles.summary: A majority of PwC India's equity partners approved a joint venture merging its consulting business with PwC US Advisory's India-based capability centre. PwC US will hold 50.1% in the new 40,000-strong JV, aiming for 5x growth and wider global client access, signaling a shift in the advisory industry playbook.

articles.headline: Emerging Markets face pressure as developed central banks hike rates
articles.summary: Developed market central banks are tightening monetary policy to combat crude-led inflation, with the US Federal Reserve, ECB, and Bank of Japan raising rates. This exerts pressure on emerging market equities and currencies. India faces increasing calls for a rate hike amidst 4.82% retail inflation and a weakening rupee.

articles.headline: Six companies to launch IPOs worth ₹3,825 crore next week
articles.summary: Six mainboard companies, including Elevate Campuses and Varmora Granito, are set to tap the primary market next week, seeking to raise a combined ₹3,825 crore through initial public offerings (IPOs). This indicates continued fundraising momentum, with 167 companies already having SEBI approval.

articles.headline: Nifty may recover after two years of underperformance: Feroze Azeez
articles.summary: Feroze Azeez, Joint CEO at Anand Rathi Wealth Ltd., believes Indian equities may recover after two years of underperformance, supported by historical returns and continued domestic institutional buying. He sees 'mean reversion' favoring India, projecting 14-15% returns over three years unless both FIIs and DIIs turn sellers.

articles.headline: DoP to curb excessive markups on hospital consumables
articles.summary: Chemicals and Fertilizers Minister J.P. Nadda has directed the Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP) to explore measures to curb excessive markups on hospital consumables. This follows a Maharashtra FDA survey revealing markups of up to 2,841% on items like IV sets and syringes, raising concerns about patient costs and regulatory gaps.

articles.headline: India's exports to core Brics markets rise 34% to $19.9 billion
articles.summary: India's exports to core Brics markets—China, South Africa, Brazil, and Russia—grew 34% to $19.9 billion in April-August 2026-27. Shipments to China jumped 39% to $9.6 billion, while South Africa recorded the fastest growth at 58%, highlighting the bloc's increasing importance for India’s export growth.

articles.headline: Retail food prices stable as production increases
articles.summary: Retail prices of key food commodities remained broadly stable in the week ended 18 September, thanks to higher foodgrain production and comfortable stock positions. Sugar prices saw the sharpest week-on-week decline (2.37%), offering some relief after August's retail inflation rose to a 20-month high of 4.82%.

articles.headline: Centre plans ₹10,000-crore push for weather forecasting modernization
articles.summary: The Centre plans a ₹10,000-crore push to modernize India's weather forecasting system by substantially expanding the Mission Mausam scheme. This includes higher outlays for new weather radars, satellites, and trained manpower, aiming for more precise forecasts amid rising extreme weather events and associated economic costs.

articles.headline: India to track seafarers globally amid West Asia conflict
articles.summary: India is developing a system for person-level tracking of its seafarers overseas, building on its existing eNavik system. This framework aims to enable quicker emergency responses by pinpointing Indian crew members, their vessels, and responsible agencies globally during conflicts or accidents, especially vital amid the West Asia war.

articles.headline: AdvaRisk nears $20 million funding with Anicut Capital interest
articles.summary: ICICI Bank-backed startup AdvaRisk, specializing in financial fraud detection and borrower risk assessment for banks, is finalizing a $20 million funding round. Anicut Capital’s growth fund is expected to join Fundamentum as an investor, with primary fundraise and secondary share sales likely to close within 20 days.

articles.headline: Corporate borrowing should shift from banks to bond market: Kotak
articles.summary: Paritosh Kashyap of Kotak Mahindra Bank asserts that a large chunk of Indian corporate borrowing must shift from bank loans to the bond market to help banks reduce direct lending exposure. India's corporate bond market, at 16% of GDP, is significantly smaller than China's (36%) or the US's (40%).

articles.headline: Defence, space sectors attract ex-govt scientists and repeat founders
articles.summary: India's push for defence indigenisation and opening of the space sector are attracting former government scientists and second-time entrepreneurs to launch ventures. Government initiatives like iDEX challenges, clear technology roadmaps, and demand for defence technologies create visible opportunities, as seen with former Isro officials founding Skyroot Aerospace.

articles.headline: Global energy supplies squeezed as refineries become chokepoint
articles.summary: Wars in Iran and Ukraine have drastically reduced refinery exports from the Middle East and Russia, causing global diesel prices to soar. With Western refineries running near capacity and limited new construction, the U.S. has become the producer of last resort, facing pressure to ban exports to lower domestic fuel costs.

articles.headline: Crypto bill collapses as industry squanders political moment
articles.summary: The landmark Clarity Act, aimed at regulating digital assets in the US, collapsed after months of negotiations. Internal industry divisions, notably Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong's withdrawal of support, and renewed ethics concerns over President Trump's crypto profits contributed to the bill's failure to advance in the Senate.

articles.headline: Infosys appoints Mitrankur Majumdar to lead SURE business unit
articles.summary: Infosys has appointed veteran Mitrankur Majumdar to lead its $2.7-billion services, utilities, resources, and energy (SURE) business, filling the position vacated by CEO-designate Ashiss Kumar Dash. This is the first major organizational change since Dash’s elevation, occurring as AI, data, and cloud reshape the IT services industry.

articles.headline: Premium content creators shift to YouTube for wider reach and IP control
articles.summary: Content creators like Balaji Telefilms are increasingly partnering with YouTube for original shows, leveraging its wider reach and ad-based monetization while retaining intellectual property. This trend reflects a shift from subscription-based streaming, driven by YouTube's massive Connected TV audience and discovery tools.

articles.headline: FMCG firms to hold prices through festive season despite rising costs
articles.summary: Fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies are likely to maintain prices through the festive season, despite rising commodity costs for sugar, edible oils, and crude derivatives. Firms aim to protect consumer demand and volume growth, having absorbed much of the inflation through cost-control initiatives and portfolio management.

articles.headline: NSE shareholders retain major stake post ₹22,569-crore IPO offer
articles.summary: A majority of existing shareholders of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) retained significant portions of their holdings even after tendering shares in the ₹22,569-crore initial public offering's offer-for-sale component. Institutional investors collectively held a 36.82% stake before the OFS.

articles.headline: Samsung's India AI appliance sales jump nine-fold
articles.summary: India has emerged as one of Samsung's fastest-growing markets for AI-powered home appliances, with newly connected devices rising nine-fold in three years to 732,000 last year. This growth, driven largely by younger consumers, increased Southwest Asia's share of Samsung connected devices worldwide to 13% in 2026.

articles.headline: Southwest monsoon begins withdrawal from west Rajasthan
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) announced that the southwest monsoon has begun withdrawing from parts of northwest India, with the withdrawal line moving across western Rajasthan. This marks the onset of the annual retreat, which typically progresses gradually towards other parts of north and central India.

articles.headline: NCLAT flags delays in NBCC's Supertech project, IRP appointment
articles.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) has raised concerns over construction major NBCC’s delay in meeting deadlines for Supertech Ltd.’s stalled housing projects. It also pulled up authorities for delaying the appointment of an interim resolution professional (IRP) for Supertech, directing NCLT and IBBI to suggest names within a week.

articles.headline: Semiconductor equipment maker ASML begins India operations
articles.summary: ASML, a leading semiconductor equipment maker, has started operations in India, planning to initially hire 20-30 engineering graduates. Its scaling-up plan depends on the success of Tata Electronics' chip unit and India's ambition to grow in the semiconductor space, as ASML's lithography technology is crucial for advanced chips.

articles.headline: Tessolve in talks to acquire two semiconductor firms
articles.summary: Semiconductor engineering services firm Tessolve, a Hero Electronix venture, is in active talks to acquire two more companies—one in the US and one in India. This move is part of its strategy to target annual revenue of over $500 million (₹4,700 crore) within the next three to four years.

articles.headline: Government operationalises ₹23,731-crore GOBARdhan scheme
articles.summary: The government has operationalised its ₹23,731-crore GOBARdhan scheme for compressed biogas (CBG) producers, offering assured offtake for up to 100% of output for 10 years and capital assistance. This aims to make waste-to-energy projects commercially viable and attract private investment for biogas and organic manure production.

articles.headline: ICAI issues new sustainability assurance standard
articles.summary: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) has issued SSA 5000, a new Standard on Sustainability Assurance, effective 1 April 2027. This standard aligns with global requirements and aims to boost confidence among investors and stakeholders regarding entities' sustainability disclosures across various topics.

articles.headline: NMDC targets 60 MT iron ore production this fiscal
articles.summary: NMDC aims to achieve 60 million tonnes (MT) of iron ore production this fiscal year to meet growing demand from domestic steelmakers. This ramp-up plan, a 20% year-on-year rise, aligns with the National Steel Policy 2017 goal of 300 MT steelmaking capacity by 2030-31.

articles.headline: EPFO wage ceiling hike impacts salary, pension, and coverage
articles.summary: The government raised the EPFO wage ceiling from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 monthly, effective 17 September. This makes EPFO mandatory for employees earning ₹15,000-₹25,000, increases maximum PF contributions to ₹3,000, and potentially boosts pension benefits to ₹13,214 monthly, affecting take-home pay and EDLI benefits.

articles.headline: Are credit card rewards worth the effort for wealth creation?
articles.summary: The author argues that the intense focus on optimizing credit card rewards for instant gratification is misplaced. Instead, allocating energy to investment fundamentals like expense ratios and asset allocation yields greater long-term financial benefits. Loyalty programs are not property; genuine wealth lies in owned assets.

articles.headline: Capital gains tax treatment for different assets
articles.summary: This table outlines the post-Budget 2024 capital gains tax treatment for various assets. Long-term capital gains (LTCG) on most assets, excluding debt funds, are now 12.5%, while short-term capital gains (STCG) on assets where STT is paid are 20%. Other assets are taxed at slab rates, with specific holding periods for LTCG.

articles.headline: Tata Sons listing path problematic amid governance dispute
articles.summary: This editorial argues that Tata Sons' path to listing, mandated by central bank rules for transparency, is problematic given the recent board vote dispute over chairman N. Chandrasekaran's reappointment. It questions the legality of board decisions defying the majority owner (Tata Trusts) and the implications for shareholder supremacy, despite the merits of transparency.

articles.headline: Managers need eightfold path for economic statecraft in new global order
articles.summary: Nitin Pai advises managers to navigate economic statecraft – the use of economic measures for political objectives – through an 'eightfold path'. This includes cultivating the right information, business mission, preparation, knowledge of global tools (tariffs, sanctions), assessment of company position, stakeholder plans, and corporate diplomacy in a changing world.

articles.headline: Government school reform emerges as a potent political issue
articles.summary: Manu Joseph argues that the dismal state of government schools in India, long an unsexy issue, is becoming a significant political idea. Exposures by movements like the Cockroach Janta Party reveal corruption and incompetence, burdening the lower middle-class and sparking widespread public discontent, making it a potential 'political tsunami'.

articles.headline: Conservatives should support ban on AI and screens in schools
articles.summary: Abby McCloskey argues that conservatives should embrace progressive-led initiatives in New York and Los Angeles to ban AI and significantly restrict screen use in public schools until high school. This 'common sense' reform aligns with concerns about falling student scores and preserving traditional learning methods amidst widespread dissatisfaction with school education quality.

articles.headline: India’s consumer market requires deep understanding beyond national averages
articles.summary: Rajesh Shukla explains that India's consumer market cannot be understood solely through national averages due to significant differences in income, consumption, and saving distribution across population deciles. Businesses must deeply understand how various households earn, spend, and retain resources to craft effective, category-specific market strategies that reach beyond affluent consumers.

articles.headline: Urban civic management failures pushing public patience to its limits
articles.summary: Rajrishi Singhal contends that urban civic management in India is in shambles, citing issues like Mumbai's budget growth not matching service quality and Bengaluru's lack of elections. He warns that public patience with shoddy delivery is wearing thin, making civic failures a potential political tsunami, drawing parallels to recent protests.

articles.headline: Companies eliminating middle management, sparking leadership shortage
articles.summary: Companies like Uber and Intel are eliminating middle management to boost efficiency, but this strategy risks creating a huge leadership shortage. The Georgetown University Center projects a 2.9 million manager shortage in the U.S. by 2032, as the unseen work of coordination and support is lost, despite the integration of AI tools.

articles.headline: For India, border peace with China comes before trade ties
articles.summary: India prioritizes border peace with China for normalising trade. Military and diplomatic talks continue amidst ongoing border issues. Bilateral trade reached $113.16 billion in FY23, but full normalization requires de-escalation of border tensions and mutual respect.

articles.headline: Tata Trusts cites SC's Cyrus Mistry ruling to counter Chandra
articles.summary: Tata Trusts referenced the Supreme Court's ruling, which upheld the removal of Cyrus Mistry, in its appeal against an attempt by Chandra to challenge the Trusts' position. The Trusts argue the SC verdict has attained finality.

articles.headline: Indian Cos poised to raise ₹1.27 lakh cr via IPOs
articles.summary: Indian companies are set to raise ₹1.27 lakh crore through IPOs, indicating a robust primary market. SEBI is streamlining processes for faster approvals, encouraging new listings and capital formation.

articles.headline: DRDO to develop powerful directed-energy weapons
articles.summary: DRDO is developing powerful directed-energy weapons (DEW) as part of a strategic initiative to enhance India's defense capabilities. The focus is on creating advanced systems for national security.

articles.headline: Medical bodies can access deceased persons' exceptional cases
articles.summary: Medical bodies can now access deceased persons' exceptional cases for research and medical advancements. This access comes with strict caveats to ensure ethical use and maintain data privacy standards.

articles.headline: SEBI board may approve tighter settlement norms
articles.summary: SEBI is expected to approve tighter settlement norms, potentially including a shorter settlement cycle (T+1). These measures aim to enhance market efficiency, protect investor interests, and reduce risks in securities transactions.

articles.headline: SEBI board to consider settlement, PMS, FPI rule changes
articles.summary: SEBI's board will meet on Sept 24 to discuss key regulatory changes. Agenda includes settlement of enforcement proceedings, new norms for Portfolio Management Services (PMS), and rules for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs).

articles.headline: Abbott India gets drug license from CDSCO
articles.summary: Abbott India received a license from CDSCO for a new drug. This approval allows the company to expand its pharmaceutical portfolio and strengthen its market presence in India.

articles.headline: Ahmednagar Multiplay gets nod to merge with Airtel
articles.summary: Ahmednagar Multiplay received regulatory approval to merge with Airtel Digital Limited. This consolidation strengthens Airtel's market presence in the region and enhances its service offerings.

articles.headline: Uttar Sibha stock climbs 19.98% on BSE
articles.summary: Uttar Sibha's stock rose significantly by 19.98% to ₹23.45 on the BSE. This surge indicates strong investor interest and positive market sentiment towards the company.

articles.headline: U.P. affirms top position in tax collection
articles.summary: Uttar Pradesh led India in state GST collection from April-August, gathering ₹45,515 crore. Karnataka and Tamil Nadu followed, collectively showcasing strong revenue generation across these major states.

articles.headline: Stellantis takes full ownership of Tiruvallur plant
articles.summary: Stellantis acquired full ownership of the Tiruvallur plant, buying out CK Birla Group's stake. This move aims to boost Stellantis' manufacturing capabilities and strengthen its market presence in India.

articles.headline: Grahaa Space accelerates Earth-observation satellites launch plans
articles.summary: Bengaluru-based Grahaa Space plans to launch Earth-observation satellite prototypes early next year using ISRO's PSLV. The initiative aims to provide high-resolution imaging services for various applications.

articles.headline: P4 poverty initiatives get around in A.P.
articles.summary: The P4 poverty alleviation program by GMR Varalakshmi Foundation has expanded its reach across Andhra Pradesh. The initiative aims to improve socio-economic conditions for distressed communities through various support programs.

articles.headline: Core tech, engineering services lift India's FY26 IT export growth
articles.summary: India's IT exports are projected to grow to $300-350 billion by FY26. This growth is primarily driven by strong demand for core technology and engineering services, despite a slowdown in software product exports.

articles.headline: OMCs recover on LPG sales; seek regular price hikes
articles.summary: Oil marketing companies (OMCs) reported recovery in LPG sales but are seeking regular price revisions. This aims to offset high input costs and reduce under-recoveries amidst volatile crude oil prices.

articles.headline: India should maintain Russian oil imports despite US pressure
articles.summary: India should continue importing discounted Russian oil, prioritizing its energy security and economic stability. External pressure from the US regarding tariffs is unwarranted, as India's foreign policy is independent.

articles.headline: Understanding permanence of life insurance benefits
articles.summary: Permanent life insurance offers lifelong coverage and builds cash value, serving as a crucial estate planning tool. It ensures financial security for beneficiaries beyond standard term coverage.

articles.headline: Shift to renewable energy, efficiency crucial for India's future
articles.summary: India needs to transition from LPG to renewable energy for cooking, promote energy efficiency, and invest in RE storage. These steps are vital for achieving energy security and environmental sustainability.

articles.headline: Saudi Arabia, Israel, US eye potential normalization deal
articles.summary: Discussions are underway for potential normalization between Saudi Arabia and Israel, brokered by the US. The complex deal involves significant geopolitical implications and challenges for regional stability.

articles.headline: Griping wives: public figures' spouses face personal challenges
articles.summary: Wives of prominent figures, including Rishi Sunak's wife and Joe Biden's daughter, are expressing personal frustrations. This highlights the private challenges faced by individuals associated with public personas.

articles.headline: Confusion at Delhi airport due to passport photo, delays
articles.summary: A chaotic situation unfolded at Delhi airport, involving an air hostess facing issues with her passport photo and flight delays, causing significant inconvenience for passengers.

articles.headline: BusinessLine bureaus enhance local news coverage
articles.summary: BusinessLine's bureaus are dedicated to enhancing local news coverage. They gather firsthand information, foster community connections, and provide diverse perspectives on regional events.

articles.headline: Review: 'Housing Republic' explores India's public housing history
articles.summary: The book "Housing Republic" reviews the evolution of public housing in India, analyzing designs, ideologies, and the socio-economic impact of government initiatives over time.

articles.headline: Review: 'A Heartbroken Country' on Afghan women under Taliban
articles.summary: The book "A Heartbroken Country" details the suffering of Afghan women under Taliban rule, exposing their loss of rights, violence, and the international community's failure to intervene effectively.

articles.headline: Food business must prioritize sustainability over economic gain
articles.summary: The food industry must shift focus from mere economic gains to sustainability, nutrition, and ethical practices. This systemic change is essential for responsible production and global well-being.

articles.headline: Indian tourist flow to Thailand unabated two decades ago
articles.summary: Twenty years ago, Indian tourist flow to Thailand remained strong and unabated, reflecting robust bilateral travel despite prevailing economic conditions.

articles.headline: RBI eased margin support on net inflows 20 years ago
articles.summary: Twenty years ago, RBI eased margin support on net inflows, indicating the central bank's efforts to manage liquidity and stabilize financial markets during that period.

articles.headline: Onida re-enters market with focus on product innovation
articles.summary: Onida, a veteran Indian electronics brand, is making a comeback by focusing on product innovation, competitive pricing, and expanding into segments like TVs, ACs, and washing machines.

articles.headline: Foldable products: from umbrellas to innovative smartphones
articles.summary: The article highlights the growing trend of foldable products, from traditional umbrellas to modern smartphones. It explores their convenience, innovative design, and expanding market presence across various sectors.

articles.headline: India's enduring love story with Brazilian football
articles.summary: India's deep passion for Brazilian football is celebrated, discussing the strong cultural connection, legendary players like Pele, and the sport's continued popularity across generations in India.

articles.headline: Iron-air batteries: cost-effective solution for solar storage
articles.summary: Form Energy, a Harvard spinoff, is developing iron-air batteries for long-duration energy storage. These cost-effective solutions aim to integrate more renewable energy like solar into electricity grids.

articles.headline: Headway in thermal hydrogen storage for renewable energy
articles.summary: Researchers are making progress in thermal hydrogen storage, developing efficient systems to store heat generated from renewable sources. This technology can reduce carbon emissions in industrial processes.

articles.headline: Caelus develops perovskite-coated glass for solar panels
articles.summary: Caelus, a US company, developed perovskite-coated glass for solar panels, achieving higher efficiency and transparency. This innovation aims to seamlessly integrate solar power into architecture and vehicles.

articles.headline: BonV Aero develops heavy-duty UAVs for high-altitude regions
articles.summary: Indian startup BonV Aero is developing heavy-duty unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for logistics and other applications in challenging high-altitude terrains, focusing on local manufacturing and advanced capabilities.

articles.headline: Conservation efforts to find mates for endangered Iberian lynx
articles.summary: The article highlights conservation efforts to find suitable mates for endangered Iberian lynx. It discusses challenges and successes in increasing their population through captive breeding and careful reintroduction programs.

articles.headline: Festival travel faces fewer seats, higher air ticket prices
articles.summary: Air tickets for festival travel are rising due to increased demand and fewer available seats. Domestic airfares are up 12-20% year-on-year, impacting holiday budgets and travel plans.

articles.headline: Trade, industry welcome Mangaluru rail freight operations rejig
articles.summary: Trade and industry bodies welcomed the railway board's decision to reallocate certain freight forwarding operations to the Mangaluru division. This move is expected to improve regional logistics and economic benefits.

articles.headline: Kirana clusters: future of inclusive retail?
articles.summary: Kirana clusters, supported by technology and efficient logistics, are emerging as a viable model for inclusive retail. They offer local communities better access to goods and generate employment opportunities.

articles.headline: FlyAsh partners with Vir India for logistics solutions
articles.summary: FlyAsh has partnered with Vir India to provide comprehensive logistics solutions. This collaboration aims to enhance and expand logistics services across Asia, Australia, and Europe.

articles.headline: Panama Canal transits drop 22% due to water scarcity
articles.summary: Panama Canal transits dropped 22% in August due to severe water scarcity. This reduction significantly impacts global shipping and supply chains.

articles.headline: Chennai Port offers waivers under PARIVARTAN scheme
articles.summary: Chennai Port Authority launched the PARIVARTAN scheme, offering waivers and incentives for cleaner cargo movement. This initiative aims to promote environmental sustainability in port operations.

articles.headline: Chennai Port to invest ₹27.50 lakh for wetland transport
articles.summary: Chennai Port Authority is set to invest ₹27.50 lakh for wetland transport infrastructure. This project aims to enhance port connectivity and efficiency.

articles.headline: Vessel with 27,000 tons of bauxite reaches Paradip Port
articles.summary: A vessel carrying 27,000 tons of bauxite from Gujarat successfully reached Paradip Port. This highlights the port's role in facilitating bulk cargo movement.

articles.headline: Indian Railways achieves record freight loading in August
articles.summary: Indian Railways achieved a record freight loading of 122.19 MT in August. This performance indicates robust activity in the national logistics sector.

articles.headline: Chennai Airport implements AAI's 'DigiYatra' for travel
articles.summary: Chennai Airport has implemented AAI's 'DigiYatra' initiative, offering seamless, paperless travel experiences for passengers. This digital service aims to enhance efficiency and convenience.

articles.headline: Ethical concerns over 'break-glass' medical data access
articles.summary: The article examines the "break-glass" allowance for medical data access without patient consent in exceptional cases. It raises ethical concerns about privacy and the need for robust safeguards.

articles.headline: Blueprint for safe, evolving AI in healthcare
articles.summary: A blueprint emphasizes ethical guidelines, data privacy, and robust regulatory frameworks for AI in healthcare. This ensures safe, effective, and responsible AI implementation in the evolving medical field.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu promotes rabies awareness on World Rabies Day
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu is observing World Rabies Day with awareness campaigns. The state promotes collaboration and vaccination efforts to eradicate rabies and educate the public.

articles.headline: Nutraceuticals gaining prominence for wellness-centric care
articles.summary: Nutraceuticals are increasingly popular for holistic health, offering therapeutic benefits beyond basic nutrition. They aim to prevent diseases and promote overall well-being, aligning with wellness-centric care trends.

articles.headline: Personal essay on training, life blueprints
articles.summary: An individual shares personal stories, including marathon training on Marine Drive, experiences with Byrox trainings, and reflections on the importance of having "blueprints" for life goals.

articles.headline: China inks MoU with UN-HABITAT for sustainable urban development
articles.summary: China's Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development signed an MoU with UN-HABITAT. The agreement aims to promote sustainable urban development globally through cooperation and knowledge sharing.

articles.headline: Ayushman Bharat scheme lacks robust emergency care component
articles.summary: The Ayushman Bharat scheme has a critical gap: a lack of a robust emergency care component. This leads to delays in accessing timely medical aid and challenges in India's healthcare system.

articles.headline: DRDO's 30 kW directed-energy weapon ready within a year
articles.summary: DRDO expects its 30 kW directed-energy weapon (DEW) to be ready for testing within a year. This advanced system aims to boost India's defense capabilities against drones and missiles.

articles.headline: Tata Sons, Trusts battle escalates to legal showdown
articles.summary: The legal dispute between Tata Sons and Tata Trusts is escalating towards a significant showdown. The battle involves key corporate governance issues and control over the long-standing family legacy.

articles.headline: Adani seeks US pre-clearance at Navi Mumbai airport
articles.summary: Adani Group is seeking US pre-clearance facilities at Navi Mumbai International Airport. This aims to streamline immigration and customs for US-bound passengers, enhancing the travel experience.

articles.headline: US and China begin high-level talks in Washington
articles.summary: US and China officials initiated high-level discussions in Washington. The talks aim to address economic and trade issues, seeking to de-escalate tensions and foster stability between the two nations.

articles.headline: Top Political Figures Hold Summit Talks
articles.summary: High-level political figures convened for crucial discussions on national policy and future strategies, signaling significant governmental initiatives and potential shifts in the political landscape. The talks covered various pressing issues.

articles.headline: Major Economic Reforms Announced by Government
articles.summary: The government unveiled a new package of economic reforms aimed at boosting growth, attracting investment, and stabilizing key financial sectors across the country. Details on fiscal measures and sectoral incentives were highlighted.

articles.headline: Key Infrastructure Projects Receive Sanction
articles.summary: Several major infrastructure development projects, including roads and energy initiatives, have received official sanction, promising significant advancements in national connectivity and power supply in coming years.

articles.headline: Health Ministry Issues New Public Guidelines
articles.summary: The Ministry of Health released updated public health guidelines concerning disease prevention and wellness programs, emphasizing community participation and access to essential healthcare services nationwide.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Delivers Landmark Ruling
articles.summary: The Supreme Court passed a significant judgment impacting property rights, setting a precedent for future legal interpretations and potentially affecting numerous ongoing cases across various states.

articles.headline: Education Sector Plans for Major Overhaul
articles.summary: Plans for a comprehensive overhaul of the national education system were revealed, focusing on curriculum modernization, teacher training, and improved access to quality learning resources.

articles.headline: New Environmental Protection Laws Enacted
